pages.text: Summer sun blazed on the shed roof. Scritch, scritch had sounded inside all morning. Grandpa hung a big cloth across the doorway.
"A gift for you, Nils. I'll show you when it's ready." Nils wanted it soon. Curiosity made his bottom wriggle.
He paced before the cloth. "Just a tiny peek. Just once."
He put his head through a gap. Wooden pieces lay in a row on the table.
A little farther, a little farther. His shoulder pushed the cloth.
Crash! The pole holding the cloth fell over. The table shook, dropping wooden pieces to the floor.
Glued joints had broken apart. Grandpa gathered the pieces one by one. Nils crouched beside him.
Grandpa glued them again. "Glue sticks while it sleeps all night. The gift needs a night's sleep too."
The next morning, Grandpa pulled back the cloth. Ta-da! A wooden horse on wheels!
Nils set it on the wooden floor. Its wheels rolled smoothly. Grandpa chuckled.
